description: How they arrived. The trap here is the resume recitation - the guest narrating a career they have already narrated many times. Every question in this pack is built to break that by asking about the parts a resume cannot hold: the misconception, the near-exit, the thing they had to unlearn.

questions.text: What did you think this job was, before you did it?
questions.lands_because: Everyone was wrong about their own field once, and the shape of that wrongness is a fast route into what the job actually is.
followups: When did you find out otherwise?

questions.text: Did you choose this, or did it accumulate?
questions.lands_because: Gives permission to skip the tidy origin myth. Most careers are drift plus one or two decisive accidents, and guests are usually relieved to be allowed to say so.

questions.text: Who was the first person you watched up close who was genuinely good at this?
questions.lands_because: Craft transmits through people, not curricula. This produces a character, a scene, and an implicit definition of excellence all at once.
followups: What did they do that you did not understand at the time?
Do you do it their way now, or did you break from it?

questions.text: What did you have to unlearn from your training?
questions.lands_because: Every field has a gap between how it teaches and how it operates. Naming the gap is insider knowledge the guest can offer without betraying anyone.
followups: Is the training still teaching that?

questions.text: Was there a point where you could have left and did not? What held you?
questions.lands_because: Reframes commitment as a decision rather than a destiny. Often the most emotionally honest moment available in the first half of an interview.
followups: Do you think you made the right call?
questions.avoid_if: The guest has just described a current crisis - it will read as a suggestion that they quit.

questions.text: Is the door into your field in the same place it was when you came through it?
questions.lands_because: Credentialing, apprenticeship, and hiring norms have shifted in nearly every industry. Experienced guests have strong, specific opinions about this and rarely get asked.
followups: Would you get hired today with the resume you had?
Is the new path better or just longer?

questions.text: What did the first year cost you that nobody warned you about?
questions.lands_because: Specific, bounded, and usually never asked. Produces concrete detail about hazing, hours, money, or the body without requiring the guest to indict anyone.
followups: Do people entering now still pay that?

setting_text.entrepreneur: What did the first year on your own cost you that nobody warned you about?
